REPORT
Date January 20, 1939.

Subject Preparation of Subversive Periodicals "Emancipation,"
"Unity", "Women" and "War Voice" - Eleven bases raided
and eighteen arrests made - Further Report

Made by D.S.I. Mac Adie Forwarded by C. Gausden

CONFIDENTIAL Interrogation of Tsai Lan ( 蔡 兰 ), important
propaganda agent for the secret national salvation
publication "Unity" has been concluded and full statement,
together with the procedure for the editing, printing and
distribution of the "Unity," which has been taken from
him, is attached as Item I of Appendix "A". In this
appendix are also included the statements of the 10th,
11th, 12th and 13th accused.

The questioning has revealed much of the organization
of national salvation propaganda in Shanghai but it would be
necessary to apprehend Pan Ts Ming ( 潘子明 ), Tsai Lan's
immediate superior to gain full details regarding the
identity of persons behind the movement. There is no doubt,
however, that this propaganda work is financed and supported
by prominent local Chinese educationalists. There is also
no doubt that the active agents find a haven in the French
Concession to carry out their plans, that material for the
publications is gathered in that district and that the agents
meet in the Concession to discuss their activities. Printing
work, however, has been carried out in the Settlement and it
is also true that the bulk of the propaganda matter finds its
way to the Settlement. In fact it may be said to follow in
the path of the educationalist, it is sent to schools through
the medium of masters or students who are members of the
Cultural or Students Circles National Salvation Associations,
to refugee camps through the refugee schools maintained in
the camps and to vocational circles and factories through

日期：1939年1月20日。

主题：颠覆性期刊《解放》、《团结》、《妇女》和《战声》的编印——突袭十一处据点并逮捕十八人——后续报告

由副督察麦阿迪（Mac Adie）撰写，由高斯登（C. Gausden）转呈

机密 对蔡兰（Tsai Lan）的审讯已结束，蔡兰是秘密抗日救国刊物《团结》的重要宣传代理人。从他那里获取的关于《团结》编辑、印刷和发行程序的完整供词，作为附件“A”的第一项附后。本附件中还包括第10、11、12和13名被告的供词。

审讯揭示了上海抗日救国宣传组织的许多情况，但有必要逮捕蔡兰的直接上级潘子明（Pan Ts Ming），才能获得关于该运动幕后人员身份的详尽细节。然而，毫无疑问，这项宣传工作是由当地著名的中国教育家资助和支持的。同样毫无疑问的是，活跃分子在法租界寻找庇护所以执行其计划，在该地区收集出版物材料，并在租界内会面讨论其活动。然而，印刷工作是在公共租界进行的，而且大部分宣传品确实流入了公共租界。事实上，可以说这些宣传品是沿着教育家的路径传播的，通过身为文化界或学生界救国会成员的教师或学生作为媒介发送到学校，通过难民营中维持的难民学校发送到难民营，并通过

for teaching and training.    The instructions to these
teachers are to use every opportunity to instil national
salvation propaganda into the refugees and imbue them with
the anti-Japanese spirit by means of lectures, dramas,
"pih pao" (wall papers), etc.

    Local national salvation elements have a federation
entitled the "Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation
Association.    In order to systematically control the various
walks of people in Shanghai, the association is divided into
the Cultural, Students, Vocation, Labourers and Women's
Circles' National Salvation Associations.

Chen）先生的名字一直出现在背景中。    可以肯定地说，国际救济委员会教育部（负责其难民营中难民的教育，由陈鹤琴先生控制）雇佣的教学和培训人员无一例外都是秘密的文化界救国会或职业界救国会的成员，这些人大多是左翼分子。    对这些教师的指示是利用一切机会，通过讲座、戏剧、“壁报”等方式，向难民灌输抗日救国宣传，使他们充满反日精神。

    本地抗日救国分子有一个联合会，名为“上海各界救国协会”。    为了系统地控制上海各界人士，该协会分为文化界、学生界、职业界、劳工界和妇女界救国会。

The magazine "Unity" is the mouthpiece of the Various
Circles National Salvation Association and the Cultural
Circles National Salvation Association was held responsible
for the publication, although all the other national
salvation circles assisted in the contributing of articles.

These national salvation associations were formed
openly following the outbreak of the hostilities in August,
1937, but as soon as the Chinese forces withdrew from
Shanghai, they became secret organizations. Even up to
the present, they still exist secretly.

Coming back to the secret publication "Unity",
which was prepared by the Cultural Circles National
Salvation Association, enquiries show that numerous persons
comprise its committees, but the majority of these people
have left Shanghai for the interior to conduct national
salvation propaganda there. Among those remaining in
Shanghai, it is known that Chang Chung-ling ( 張采麟 ),
Liang Sz-jung ( 梁士純 ), and Pan Ts-ming alias Pan Fang
( 潘芳 ) are the leading members. Pan Ts-ming is the
direct chief of Tsai Lan (15th accused) and is the Chief of
the Propaganda Department. This man disappeared after the
arrest of the 15th accused and before the Police visit at
his home at Lane 559-B, 11 Rue Lafayette.

Chang Chung-ling is known to be a teacher in the
Chung Hwa No.4 Vocational School, Pootung Guild Building,
1454 Avenue Edward VII, but enquiries show that he has not
put in an appearance there since the arrest of Tsai Lan.

杂志《团结》是各界救国协会的喉舌，虽然其他所有救国界别都协助供稿，但出版责任由文化界救国会承担。

这些救国协会在1937年8月战事爆发后公开成立，但随着中国军队撤离上海，它们随即转为秘密组织。即使到现在，它们仍然以秘密形式存在。

回到由文化界救国会准备的秘密刊物《团结》，调查显示其委员会由众多人员组成，但其中大多数人已离开上海前往内地，在那里进行抗日救国宣传。在留在上海的人员中，已知张采麟（Chang Chung-ling）、梁士纯（Liang Sz-jung）和潘子明（又名潘芳，Pan Fang）是主要成员。潘子明是第15名被告蔡兰的直接上司，也是宣传部主任。此人在第15名被告被捕后、警方前往其位于拉斐德路（Rue Lafayette）559-B弄的住所之前失踪。

已知张采麟是浦东同乡会大楼（爱多亚路1454号）中华第四职业学校的教师，但调查显示，自蔡兰被捕以来，他未再出现在该校。

According to Tsai Lan, he was responsible only for
the magazine "Unity", the mouthpiece of the Cultural Circles
National Salvation Association. Although the printing of
the other publications, "War Voice", "Emancipation" and
"Women" was done through the Medhurst Road base, arrange-
ments for this were made by Pan Ts Ming direct. "Emancipation",
the communist journal, is said to be published in Shensi, seat
of the Communist Anti-Japanese University ( 抗日大学 )
and is only reproduced in Shanghai. As regards "Women,"
the 16th accused Pan Kwoh Tseng-yih, wife of Pan Ts Ming,
and the 1st accused Sung Yue ( 沈裕 ) who were arrested
at Lane 559-B, 11 Rue Lafayette and later released, together
with Tsai Ying, a cousin of Tsai Lan's, and Woo Sui-tsing
( 吴水清 ), the latter's sweetheart and a teacher at the
1st Refugee Camp of the International Relief Committee, are
actively engaged in its production. The magazine is the
mouthpiece of the Women's Circles National Salvation
Association headed by Miss Huang Ting Wei.

In the possession of Tsai Lan (15th accused) were
found two booklets containing notes on minutes of secret
meetings held by the committee members of the Women's

notes, it has been gathered that the following females

Apart from the usual organization, the Women's
Circles National Salvation Association has a Liaison
Department and a Refugee Education Department, which shows ||
that women agitators are also paying much attention towards
influencing the refugees. The following activities are
found recorded in the notes of minutes of the secret
meetings :-

1. Holding of a national goods exhibition.

2. Collecting of contributions from local women for the
   upkeep of the secret magazine entitled "Unity."

3. Investigating of shops and firms dealing in Japanese
   goods.

4. Launching of the "Returning to Native Place" and "Thrift"
   movement (the latter movement to be carried out openly
   by the Women's Christian Temperance Association, 50
   Love Lane).

    In connection with this case, eleven places were
raided by the Municipal Police in the International
Settlement and in the French Concession with the assistance
of the French Police.    Communistic and subversive
literature and propaganda were found in nine of these
places, while five places were closed down by the Municipal
Police for being concerned in the type-setting, making of
matrices and printing of the subversive publications
"Emancipation," "Unity," "Women" and "War Voice". Two of
these five places were allowed to re-open on the instructions
of D.C. (Special Branch), the types of one secret type-setting
base(established for these publications only and no other
business) are now detained at Police Headquarters pending
instructions, while the remaining two, the Lien Ta Type-
setting Works and the Shing Nyih Press, remain closed.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
S.1, Special Branch **〔此处转录不清〕**
REPORT    Date January 12, 1939.

Subject Secret National Salvation Publications - Release of
accused on bond **〔此处有手写插入符号及字迹，难以辨认〕**

Made by D.S.I. Mac Adie    Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.J.

The 8th accused Tsang Vung Sing (張文心),
apprentice of the secret type setting base at Lane 597,
No.7 Medhurst Road was released on the afternoon of
January 11 on guarantee bond supplied by his grand-father
named Tsang Moh-ling (張木林), master of the Tsang
Zung Shing (張順兴) Cotton Shop, 239 Weihaiwei Road.
The youth is being sent to join his father in their country
home at Pootung.

The 5th and 6th accused, Wong Dzu Chi (王樹基)
and Fang Yue-keng (方友根), also apprentices of the
above base were released on the morning of January 12th.
Bond for the first named was supplied by Kan Zien-keng
(甘泉根), his cousin and a foreman employed by the
Nyi Sung (義生) Rubber Factory, 83 Penang Road. The
second named was released on guarantee supplied by Yue
Chia Toong (余家棟), the electrician of the Cotton
Goods Exchange, 260 Avenue Edward VII.

Wong Dzu Chi is being sent to join his parents in
his native home near Kading. The last named Fang Yue Keng
will remain with his guarantor and father named Fang Ching-
sung (方金生), a hawker, at the Cotton Goods Exchange.

Before release the three apprentices and their
guarantors were given a strict caution against the former
re-engaging in subversive activities.

R.W. Mac Adie
D. S. I.

第八被告张文心（Tsang Vung Sing），麦赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）597弄7号
秘密排版基地的学徒，于1月11日下午由其祖父张木林（Tsang Moh-ling）
提供担保债券获释，张木林系威海卫路239号张顺兴（Tsang Zung Shing）
棉布店店主。该青年将被送往浦东家乡与其父亲团聚。

第五和第六被告，王树基（Wong Dzu Chi）和方友根（Fang Yue-keng），
也是上述基地的学徒，于1月12日上午获释。前者的担保人是其表亲
甘泉根（Kan Zien-keng），系槟榔路83号义生（Nyi Sung）橡胶厂领班。
后者由爱德华七世路（Avenue Edward VII）260号棉业交易所电工余家栋
（Yue Chia Toong）提供担保获释。

王树基将被送往嘉定附近的家乡与其父母团聚。最后一位方友根将与其
担保人及父亲方金生（Fang Ching-sung，小贩）一同留在棉业交易所。

在释放之前，已对这三名学徒及其担保人提出严厉警告，禁止前者再次
从事颠覆活动。

R.W. Mac Adie
副督察长（D. S. I.）

Seizures etc. - Further Report
Made by D.S.I. Mac Adie    Forwarded by **〔签名：C. Crawford. S. I〕**

Lan Chung-siang (藍仲祥), who was arrested at
Passage 559-B, No.11 Rue Lafayette on the night of January
4th and handed over to Special Branch was on the instructions
of D.C. (Special Branch) returned to the Political Section,
French Police on the morning of January 7th from where he
was subsequently released.

The Han Wen Press, Lane 228, No.15 Shantung Road,
which was ordered to cease operations on November 30th
was on January 4th authorized to re-open by D.C. (Special
Branch) after suitable guarantees had been supplied by
Mr. Sung Kwang-dee (孙光弟), Manager of the Sun Sun
Press (生生美術公司), 105 Lloyd Road, against the former
concern again engaging in the printing or preparation of
subversive literature.

The Dah Foong Type-Setting Works, Lane 537, No.6
Wuting Road, the operation of which was suspended on
December 6th were permitted to re-open by D.C. (Special
Branch) on January 6th. Suitable guarantees against this
concern re-engaging in the preparation of subversive
literature were entered into by Mr. Wei Tse-hung (韋志宏),
master of the Tse Zung (志成) Rice Shop, Lane 779, No.53
Chengtu Road.

The guarantee bonds for the Han Wen Press and
Dah Foong Works are attached.

**〔左侧批注：8/1〕**

**〔签名：R.W. Mac Adie.〕**
D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch).

蓝仲祥（Lan Chung-siang，藍仲祥），于1月4日晚在拉斐德路（Rue Lafayette）11号559-B弄被捕并移交特务科，根据特务科副主任的指示，已于1月7日上午交还法国警察厅政治科，随后获释。

汉文印刷所，位于山东路15号228弄，曾于11月30日被勒令停业，在生生美术公司（Sun Sun Press，地址劳合路105号）经理孙光弟（Sung Kwang-dee，孙光弟）提供适当担保，保证该商号不再从事颠覆性刊物的印刷或制作后，特务科副主任于1月4日批准其重新开业。

大丰制版所，位于武定路6号537弄，曾于12月6日暂停营业，特务科副主任于1月6日准许其重新开业。成都路53号779弄志成米店主人韦志宏（Wei Tse-hung，韋志宏）已签署适当担保，保证该商号不再从事颠覆性刊物的制作。

汉文印刷所和大丰制版所的担保书附后。

released same evening. In connection with the 17th
accused Lan Chung Ziang (藍仲祥), who is a teacher
in the Chung Hwa Girls' Middle School, Rue Lafayette,
although he admits that he was a close friend of the
wanted man Pan Ts Ming and allowed Pan the use of his
desk, he denies being concerned with the production of
the magazines "Unity" etc. Lan Chung Ziang is not
identified by Tsai Lan or Bang Yue Zung, the 3rd accused
as being connected with the movement while his name does
not appear on any of the documents seized. In the
absence of evidence of any subversive activities on the
part of Lan Chung Ziang, his release would appear advisable.

With reference to Pan Ts Ming, evidence has been
secured that this man absconded during the day of January 4,
his home being raided that evening. By some means or other
he apparently learned of the arrest of Tsai Lan and has gone
into hiding.

A list of the literature seized in the recent
raids is in course of preparation and will be forwarded
as soon as possible.

R.W. Mac Adie
D. S. I.

Made by D.S.I. MacAdie Forwarded by C. Crawford. S.I.

Tsai Lan (蔡磊) alias Li Ts Ming (李子民),
age 26, native of Canton, who was implicated by the 3rd and
4th accused in the case which forms the subject of this
file, as being the responsible person behind the secret
type setting base at Lane 587, No.7 Medhurst Road, from
whom the drafts of the objectionable publications, Unity,
etc. emanated and by whom the distribution of these
periodicals was conducted, was as a result of careful
enquiries traced to his home in Room No.4 of a Russian
Boarding House, Lane 697, No.5 Avenue Joffre.

This address was raided by D.S.I. MacAdie, D.S.I.
Kao Yen-ken and C.D.S.156 (Special Branch) assisted by
D.S.I. Perrie of the Political Section, French Police, at
7.30 a.m. January 4 and the wanted man was taken into
custody therein.

A quantity of manuscripts and literature believed
to be chiefly of a national salvation nature was seized
and is at present under examination.

Tsai Lan was handed over to Special Branch at
10 a.m. same day, for enquiries, on the understanding that
should his expulsion from Shanghai be later deemed
desirable, this be carried out by the French Police owing
to his being a resident of the Concession.

Tsai Lan who now becomes the 17th accused in this
case is being carefully interrogated with a view to tracing
the organization at the back of the propaganda matter in
question.

He will be detained in Central Station.

R.W. Mac...
D.C. (Special Branch)

蔡磊（Tsai Lan），别名李子民（Li Ts Ming），
26岁，广东人，在本案第3和第4被告的供词中被牵连，据称是麦特赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）7号587弄秘密排版基地背后的负责人，违禁刊物《团结》等的草稿即出自该处，且这些期刊的分发亦由其负责。经过仔细调查，追踪到其住所位于霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）5号697弄一家俄国人寄宿处的4号房间。

1月4日上午7时30分，副督察 MacAdie、副督察 Kao Yen-ken（音译）和特别分部刑事侦探长156号（C.D.S.156）在法国警察政治科副督察 Perrie 的协助下突袭了该地址，并将该通缉犯当场拘捕。

查获了大量手稿和文献，据信主要为救国性质，目前正在审查中。

蔡磊于当日上午10时移交给特别分部进行讯问，鉴于其为法租界居民，若日后认为将其驱逐出上海为宜，将由法国警察执行驱逐。

蔡磊现成为本案第17名被告，正受到仔细审问，以期查明上述宣传事项背后的组织。

他将被关押在中央巡捕房。

Works, Lane 140, House 15 Love Lane was visited and all
work ordered to cease. The responsible persons were
taken into custody. They are :-

(10th accused): Chu Han Sung( 朱杏生 ), aged 37,
a native of Shanghai, married, Manager
& Owner of the Lien Ts Type-Setting
Works. Living at the said address.

(11th accused): Liu Dong Hui( 劉全煥 ), aged 22,
a native of Ningpo, married, broker of
the Lien Ts Type-Setting Works.
Living at the said address.

A search of the premises revealed a quantity of
anti-Japanese books, manuscript and matrices, a description
of which is given in the attached list. The source of
this literature is under investigation.

At 11 a.m. the Shing Nyih Press( 兴业 ), Lane
177, House 42 Chungking Road was similarly ordered to cease
operations and the responsible persons were taken into
custody. They are :-

(12th accused): Loh Ching Yeong( 陸金榮 ), aged 51,
a native of Kashan, Chekiang, married.
Manager of the Shing Nyih Press.
Living at the said address.

关于此前在12月16日关于此主题的报告中提到的两家剩余印刷和排版厂，它们曾从事印刷或制作各种性质违禁的秘密出版物的母版，根据助理处长（特别分部）的指示，警方于12月23日对其采取了行动。

上午10时，警方走访了位于爱文义路（Love Lane）140弄15号的利志（Lien Ts）排版厂，并命令停止所有工作。负责人被拘捕。他们是：

（第10名被告）：朱杏生（Chu Han Sung），37岁，上海人，已婚，利志排版厂经理兼业主。居住于上述地址。

（第11名被告）：劉全煥（Liu Dong Hui），22岁，宁波人，已婚，利志排版厂经纪人。居住于上述地址。

对该场所的搜查发现了大量反日书籍、手稿和母版，其描述见附单。这些文献的来源正在调查中。

上午11时，同样命令位于重庆路（Chungking Road）177弄42号的兴业（Shing Nyih）印刷所停止运营，并将负责人拘捕。他们是：

（第12名被告）：陸金榮（Loh Ching Yeong），51岁，浙江嘉善（Kashan，音译）人，已婚。兴业印刷所经理。居住于上述地址。

Assistant Manager of the Shing Nyih
Press. Living in the Press. Son
of Loh Ching Yoong.

Nothing was found on the premises but the manager
was unable to produce his account books for the year 1938,
having only a set of books dated from August 1938 which bore
every evidence of their having been written up at a very
recent date. The manager admitted that news of the raid
on the Han Wen Press on November 30th had come to his
notice and it is evident that he either concealed or
destroyed the old books which contained records of his
transactions with the 3rd and 4th accused. Investigations
into this matter will be made in due course.

The four arrested persons are at present being
detained in Chengtu Road Station.

Arrangements have been made by P.A. to D.C.
(Special Branch) with the Inspector in charge of Chengtu
Road Station for the policing of the two concerns with
a view to ensuring that work is not resumed.

With reference to the Sung Wah ( 生活 ) Bookstore,
c/o Yuan Tung ( 遠東 ) Bookstore, 378 Foochow Road which
ordered a quantity of rabidly anti-Japanese cartoons and
songs from the Han Wen Press, discreet enquiries ascertained
that the Yuan Tung Bookstore is entirely responsible for
all Shanghai affairs of the Sung Wah Bookstore which is
stated to be now located at Queens Road Hongkong.

December 23, 1938.

To the Special Branch, S.M.P.

My client, Mr. Zee Sing Zu (徐心如),
proprietor of the Da Foong Type Manufacturing Co., states
that one of his workers named Wong Ching Kung was arrested
by Special Branch detectives on December 1 and the company
was ordered to suspend work on the following day, Dec. 2.
Policemen are watching the premises daily. It is not known
what offence Wong Ching Kung has committed, but anyhow this
concerns Wong himself and has nothing to do with my client's
company, which has suffered a great loss through suspension
of work. A letter was forwarded sometime ago requesting
permission to re-open the shop but no reply has been received.
Accordingly he requests me to write to you again with a view
to permitting him to resume business as soon as possible in
order to avoid further losses.

Shen Ying Shih
Attorney-At-Law.

D.S.J. Macrae
E 24/12.

1938年12月23日。

致上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处。

我的当事人，大丰字模制造公司（Da Foong Type Manufacturing Co.）业主徐心如（Zee Sing Zu）先生称，其一名名为王敬功（Wong Ching Kung）的工人于12月1日被特别处侦探逮捕，该公司随后于次日即12月2日被勒令停工。警察每日监视该场所。尚不清楚王敬功犯有何种罪行，但无论如何，此事仅涉及王本人，与我的当事人的公司无关，而公司因停工遭受了巨大损失。此前曾去信请求准许重新开业，但未获回复。因此，他委托我再次致函贵处，恳请准许其尽快恢复营业，以避免进一步损失。

沈英士
律师。

At 10 a.m. on 23-12-38 D.S.I.s MacAdie, Kao Yeu Keng, C.D.S. 156 and C.D.C. 362 raided the Lieu Ts Pringing Factory (聯智) at 15/140 Love Lane and seized a quantity of literature of anti-Japanese nature. Two named Ta Hung Sung (朱杏生), age 37, Shanghai, and Liu Toong Wen (刘同炳), 22, Ningpo, Manager and Broker of the above Factory respectively were placed into custody and brought to this Station.

At 11 a.m. same morning the same party of detectives attached to Special Branch accompanied by C.D.C. 26 and the undersigned raided the Shing Yih Printing Factory (兴業.), at 42/177 Chungking Road, where the Manager named Loh Kyung Yoong (羅金榮), age 51, Shanghai, and an assistant Loh Foh Sung (陸福生), age 30, Shanghai, were arrested and a number of account books seized. No literature of incriminating nature was found on the premises.

The above four Arrested persons are being detained at this Station pending further instructions from D.C. (Special Branch).

The above two factories were ordered to cease operating their business by D.C. (Special Branch).

Interrogation of the eight accused now in custody
in connection with this case has now been completed.
As a result of the arrest of Ghui Pah-lee ( 瞿 柏 礼 ),
the 9th accused, it was discovered that one Tsai Lan
( 蔡 磊 ) alias Li Yah-yuin ( 李 雅 雲 ), a teacher
in the 1st Refugee Camp of the International Relief
Committee, Rue Massenet and a staff member of the Moral
Training Committee was the responsible figure behind the
secret type setting base at Medhurst Road. Enquiries
at the camp ascertained that since the raid he had absented
himself on sick leave and further interrogation of the
prisoners ascertained that the 9th accused had witnessed
the arrest of the 3rd accused on December 1st at the Han
Wen Press and had immediately left to warn Tsai Lan.
The 9th accused also attempted to warn the employees of
the type setting base to abscond and remove the types but
in this he was too late. Tsai Lan's residence is not known
to the accused but careful enquiries are being continued in
an effort to effect his arrest. Not only did the drafts of
the various objectionable secret publications emanate from
him but he is also stated to have financed the purchase of
the type and fittings of the base and to have made a
regular monthly allowance to the accused. The length of
time which this secret base operated undisturbed and
unsuspected i.e. from May to December is evidence of the
success of the scheme. Type setting is the longest
operation in printing and necessitates the presence of

与此案有关的八名在押被告的审讯现已完成。由于第九名被告瞿伯礼（Ghui Pah-lee）的被捕，发现马思南路国际救济委员会第一难民营的一名教师、道德励志委员会的工作人员蔡磊（Tsai Lan），又名李雅云（Li Yah-yuin），是梅赫斯特路秘密排版基地背后的负责人。在该难民营进行的查询查明，自突袭以来，他以病假为由缺席。对囚犯的进一步审讯查明，第九名被告曾目睹第三名被告于12月1日在汉文印刷社被捕，并立即离开去警告蔡磊。第九名被告还试图警告排版基地的员工潜逃并移除字模，但为时已晚。被告不知晓蔡磊的住所，但正在继续仔细查询以设法将其逮捕。不仅各种违禁秘密出版物的草稿出自他手，据称他还资助购买了该基地的字模和设备，并向被告定期发放月度津贴。该秘密基地在未受干扰且未被怀疑的情况下运作的时间长度，即从五月到十二月，证明了该计划的成功。排版是印刷过程中耗时最长的工序，需要

department of the local National Salvation and leftist

Propaganda Matter handled

"Emancipation" ( 解 放 ),
a semi-monthly periodical of a purely
communistic nature having strong anti-
Japanese tendency.

"Unity" ( 团 结 ),
a weekly periodical of an anti-Japanese
and national salvation nature, the mouth-
piece of local national salvation elements.

"War Voice" ( 战 声 ),
a three-day periodical of an anti-Japanese
and national salvation nature, bearing on
the war situation.

"Women" ( 妇 女 ),
a semi-monthly periodical of an anti-Japanese
and national salvation nature, the mouth-piece
of the local women national salvation circles.

"Students' Livelihood" ( 学 生 生 活 ),
a semi-monthly periodical of an anti-Japanese
and national salvation nature, the mouth-piece
of the secret "Students' Federation" (for one
issue only in August, 1936).

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Wong Chi-gee ( 王 企 岐 ) (1st accused)
native of Shaoshing taken by me D.S.I. MacAdie
D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken
at Special Branch on the 13/12/38 and interpreted by

My name is Wong Chi-gee. I am 41 years of age,
a native of Shaoshing, and married. I reside at 59, Yung
Chih Li ( 永 吉 里 ), Elgin Road, off North Kiangse Road.
I am the Sales Manager of the Han Wen Press, Lane 228, 15
Shantung Road.

This press was responsible for the printing of the
"War Voice" from August up to the date on which the Municipal
Police raided the Press for the periodical. The work was
introduced to me by Wong Kyung-kung (4th accused). Wong
was an apprentice and I was an accountant in the Mei Shen
( 美 成 ) Press, Yu Ching Li, corner of East Seward Road
and Singkeepang Road, in 1931. The set-up types of the
"War Voice" were as a rule sent to my press by Bang Yuen
Shen (3rd accused) and the printed copies were taken away
by persons sent by Bang who are unknown to me. The cost
of the printing was collected by Wong Kyung-kung (4th
accused) from Bang (3rd accused) and sent to me. Wong got
a commission of $0.30 out of a total price of $1.60 per
issue.

This press also printed the "July 7th Anniversary
Special Issue" of the Communistic periodical "Emancipation."
As the printing proved unsatisfactory, Bang discontinued to
send further issues to us for printing. I deny having
printed two issues of "Emancipation" and one issue of
"Unity" as claimed by Bang Yuen-shen (3rd accused).

The set-up types for the "Anti-Japanese Songs"
which were seized from the press by the Municipal Police

警方调查报告。

以下是由我，警司 MacAdie，
警司 Kao Yen-ken，
于1938年12月13日在特别支部对第一被告王企岐 (Wong Chi-gee)，绍兴籍人士进行的讯问陈述，并由____翻译

我叫王企岐。现年41岁，绍兴籍，已婚。我居住在江西北路附近的埃尔金路 (Elgin Road) 永吉里59号。我是山东路15号228弄汉文印刷所的销售经理。

该印刷所负责从八月起至工部局警察搜查该期刊之日止印刷《战声》。这项工作是由王金根（第四被告）介绍给我的。1931年，王是学徒，我是会计师，我们都在东熙华德路与新加坡路 (Singkeepang Road) 拐角处的余庆里美成 (Mei Shen) 印刷所工作。《战声》的排好版的活字通常由彭元成（第三被告）送到我的印刷所，印好的刊物则由彭派来的我不认识的人取走。印刷费用由王金根（第四被告）从彭（第三被告）处收取后转交给我。王从每期1.60美元的总价中抽取0.30美元作为佣金。

该印刷所还印刷了共产主义期刊《解放》的“七七周年纪念特刊”。由于印刷效果不尽如人意，彭便不再将后续期数送来给我们印刷。我否认曾按彭元成（第三被告）所称印刷过两期《解放》和一期《团结》。

被工部局警察从印刷所查获的《抗日歌曲》的排好版的活字

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Loo Chieu-sung (羅秋生) (2nd accused)
native of Shanghai taken by me D.S.I. MacAdie
at Special Branch on the 13/12/38 and interpreted by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken

My name is Loo Chieu-sung. I am 45 years of age,
a native of Shanghai and married. I reside at 6 Shih Sing
Li (石新里), Route Pere Robert. I am the Works Manager
of the Han Wen Press, Lane 228, 15 Shantung Road. I am one
of the three shareholders of this press, the other two being
Wong Chi-gee (1st accused) and Sung Pah-an.

The anti-Japanese and national salvation literature
and blocks seized by the Municipal Police from the press
were received by Wong Chi-gee and various brokers in the
trade.

Although I was aware that such literature was
undesirable I offered no objection to its being printed
as the other business was not sufficient to maintain the
press.

I do not know who ordered the printing and the
making of matrices in this case.

以下是由我，警司 MacAdie，于1938年12月13日在特别支部对第二被告罗秋生 (Loo Chieu-sung)，上海籍人士进行的讯问陈述，并由警司 Kao Yen-ken 翻译

我叫罗秋生。现年45岁，上海籍，已婚。我居住在贝当路 (Route Pere Robert) 石新里6号。我是山东路15号228弄汉文印刷所的工场经理。我是该印刷所的三位股东之一，另外两位是王企岐（第一被告）和沈百先。

被工部局警察从该印刷所查获的抗日及救国文献和印版是由王企岐以及行业内的各类掮客接收的。

虽然我知道此类文献是不受欢迎的，但由于其他业务不足以维持印刷所的运营，我对其印刷并未提出异议。

我不知道在此案中是谁下令进行印刷和制作纸型的。

The following is the statement of Pang Yuen-shen (3rd accused)

My name is Pang Yuen-shen (彭元成), alias Pang
Jen-sung (彭仁生), alias Chang Shen-kao (張成高).
I am 32 years of age, a native of Shaoshing, and married.
I am a type-setter by profession and reside at Lane 587, 7
Medhurst Road. The kitchen room of this address is used
by me and Ghui Pah-li (瞿伯礼) (9th accused) as a
secret type-setting base for the communistic and anti-Japanese
publications "Unity", "War Voice", "Emancipation" and
"Women".
Prior to April, 1938, I was employed in the Tai Ping
Yang Printing Press, Lane 161, 11 Burkill Road, as a type-
setter and was discharged in March following a raid on the
press by the Municipal Police for anti-Japanese literature.
In April, 1938, Tsai Lan (蔡磊), alias Li Yah-yuin
(李雅雲), who ordered the printing of the "Unity" from
the Tai Ping Yang Press, approached me and Ghui and suggested
the establishment of a secret type-setting base for the
above-mentioned four secret publications. He gave us $200
for the purchase of types and in May, we rented the kitchen
room of Lane 587, 7 Medhurst Road, as the works. The
staff consisted of six persons, namely, Ghui and I as type-
setters, Wang Dau-shi (王如寺)(5th accused), Fang Yu-
heng (方餘根)(6th accused) and Tsang Yung-tsing (8th
accused) as apprentices, and my wife Pang Chang Da (彭張氏)
as the cook. For our support, Tsai Lan paid $45.00 per
person, of which sum, $36 was set aside for food and the
remaining 9 for the miscellaneous expenses.

以下是由我，警司 MacAdie，
警司 Kao Yen-ken，
于1938年12月8日在总部对第三被告彭元成 (Pang Yuen-shen)，绍兴籍人士进行的讯问陈述，并由____翻译

我叫彭元成，别名彭仁生 (Pang Jen-sung)，别名张成高 (Chang Shen-kao)。现年32岁，绍兴籍，已婚。我职业为排字工人，居住在麦赫斯特路 (Medhurst Road) 7号587弄。该地址的厨房房间被我与瞿伯礼 (Ghui Pah-li)（第九被告）用作共产主义及抗日出版物《团结》、《战声》、《解放》和《妇女》的秘密排版基地。
1938年4月之前，我在伯基尔路 (Burkill Road) 11号161弄太平洋印刷所担任排字工人，在该印刷所因抗日文献被工部局警察搜查后，于次年三月被解雇。
1938年4月，曾向太平洋印刷所订购《团结》印刷业务的蔡磊 (Tsai Lan)，别名李雅雲 (Li Yah-yuin)，找到我和瞿，建议为上述四种秘密出版物建立一个秘密排版基地。他给了我们200美元用于购买铅字，5月份，我们租下了麦赫斯特路7号587弄的厨房房间作为工场。工作人员共六人，即我和瞿担任排字工，王如寺 (Wang Dau-shi)（第五被告）、方餘根 (Fang Yu-heng)（第六被告）和曹永清 (Tsang Yung-tsing)（第八被告，音译）担任学徒，以及我的妻子彭张氏 (Pang Chang Da) 担任厨师。为了维持我们的生活，蔡磊每人支付45.00美元，其中36美元用于伙食，剩余的9美元用于杂项开支。

I was in charge of the works, while Ghui (9th accused)
served as a communication agent between the works and Tsai
Lan. I was also responsible for the taking of the set up
types to the Han Wen Printing Press, Lane 228, 15 Shantung
Road, for printing. The Han Wen Printing Press has
undertaken the printing since May, 1938. When printed,
the publications were removed from the Han Wen Press by

kyūng-keng (王金根)(4th accused), worker in the Dah Foong
(大豐) Press, Lane 537, 6 Wuting Road, with Wang Chi-gae
(1st accused), Manager of the Sales Department of the Han
Wen Press.

As to the paper matrices which were seized by the
Municipal Police at Lane 567, 7 Medhurst Road, I have to
state that they were made at the Dah Foong Press, Lane 537,
6 Wuting Road, at the rate of $0.36 a copy.

I know that Tsai Lan is a teacher in the 1st Refugee
Camp of the International Relief Committee, Rue Massanet.
Tsai Lan's activities and whereabouts have been kept strictly
secret from us. I am not clear as to whether he belongs
to the Chinese Communist Party or the "National Salvation
Association". Besides Tsai Lan, one Pan Ta-ming (潘大明)
came to proof read the "Unity" and "Women", one Foo Ching-
yoong (傅金榮) to read the proof of "War Voice" and one
Yu Ying-sung (余蔭生) to see the "Emancipation" for the
final time. Their identity is unknown to me.

At 11 a.m., December 1, an employee of the Han Wen Press

The following further statement of Pang Yuen-shen (3rd accused) ( 彭元成 )

My name is Pang Yuen-shen alias Pang Jen-sung ( 彭仁生 ),
alias Chang Shen-kao ( 張成高 ). I am 32 years of age, a
native of Shaoshing, and married. The following is my
further statements:-

The types of all the four periodicals entitled "Unity",
"Emancipation", "War Voice" and Women", were set up at the
Medhurst Road base, but the printing was done by the
following two firms:-

a) Han Wen Press, Lane 228, 15 Shantung Road.
Responsible for the printing of the "War Voice" from
July, 1938 up to the present.
Printed one issue of the "Unity" and two issues of the
"Emancipation" in July.

b) Shing Nyi Press ( 兴业 ), Lane 177, 42 Chungking Rd.
Responsible for the printing of the "Unity", "Women"
and the "Emancipation" from May, 1938, up to the present.

With regard to the making of matrices for the "Women",
"Emancipation" and "Unity", I have to state that it was
done by the Dah Foong Type-setting Works ( 大丰 ), Lane
587, 6 Wuting Road, in May, June, July and August, 1938.
Then we secured the services of the Lien Ts ( 利兹 ) Type-
setting Works, Love Lane, behind the Bank of China Building,
which charged $0.32 for each matrix instead of $0.36 as
charged by the Dah Foong, and therefore we entrusted the
work with the new firm. This Lien Ts Works has been
responsible for the making of matrices since the beginning
of September, 1938.

--------

以下是由我，警司 MacAdie，于1938年12月13日在警察总部对第三被告彭元成 ( 彭元成 )，绍兴籍人士进行的进一步讯问陈述，并由____翻译

我叫彭元成，别名彭仁生 ( 彭仁生 )，别名张成高 ( 張成高 )。现年32岁，绍兴籍，已婚。以下是我的进一步陈述：-

名为《团结》、《解放》、《战声》和《妇女》的所有四种期刊的活字均在麦赫斯特路基地排版，但印刷工作由以下两家商号完成：-

a) 汉文印刷所，山东路15号228弄。
负责自1938年7月起至今印刷《战声》。
7月份印刷了一期《团结》和两期《解放》。

b) 兴业印刷所 ( Shing Nyi Press )，重庆路42号177弄。
负责自1938年5月起至今印刷《团结》、《妇女》和《解放》。

关于为《妇女》、《解放》和《团结》制作纸型一事，我必须说明，这是由大丰排版社 ( Dah Foong Type-setting Works )（武定路6号587弄，音译注：原文此处门牌与前文大丰印刷所不同，照实译出）在1938年5月、6月、7月和8月完成的。随后，我们雇佣了位于中国银行大楼背后爱文义路的利兹 ( Lien Ts ) 排版社，其每副纸型收费0.32美元，而非大丰收取的0.36美元，因此我们将工作委托给了这家新商号。自1938年9月初以来，该利兹排版社一直负责制作纸型。

--------

The following is the statement of Wong Kyung Kung (王金根), (4th accused)
native of Kiangwan taken by me D.S.I. MacAdie
at Police Hqrs. on the Dec. 9, 1938 and interpreted by ~~D.S.I. Kao Yen Kung~~

My name is Wong Kyung-kung. I am 26 years of age,
a native of Kiangwan, and married. I am a matrix maker
in the employ of the Dah Foong (大豐) Type-setting
Works, sponsored by the Commercial Press, Lane 537, 6
Wuting Road. I reside in a country house No. 41 Siao
Woo Ka Zah(小胡家宅), Jessfield Road, at the rear of St.
John's University, O.O.L.

In May, 1938, while I was residing at 12 Ching Wei
Li (駿蔚里), opposite Lane 587, 7 Medhurst Road, I made
acquaintance with Bang Yuen-shen(彭元成)(3rd accused).
He asked me to introduce some printing firm to him. The
type-setting base at Lane 587, 7 Medhurst Road, which was
operated by Bang, did not carry out any business other than
for the following secret publications:-
War Voice (戰声),
Unity (团结),
Emancipation(解放),
Women (婦女).

Thereupon I went to see Wong Chi-gee (1st accused),
Manager of the Printing Department of the Han Wen Press.
Wong became known to me while he was serving as the
accountant and I as an apprentice in the Mei Shen (美成)
Press, Yu Ching Li(餘慶里), corner of East Seward Road
and Singkeapang Road, in 1931. Wong accepted the
business. Besides introducing the business of printing,
I have nothing to do with the secret publications.

As to the making of matrices of these publications,

本人名叫王金根。现年26岁，江湾人，已婚。本人系受雇于大丰排字馆的制模工人，该馆由商务印书馆资助，位于吴淞路6号537弄。本人居住于圣约翰大学后方、极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）小胡家宅41号的一间乡间房屋内，门牌号为O.O.L.。

1938年5月，本人居住在麦赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）7号587弄对面的骏蔚里12号时，结识了彭元成（Bang Yuen-shen）（第三被告）。他请本人向他介绍一些印刷厂商。由彭在麦赫斯特路7号587弄经营的排字基地，除为下列秘密刊物进行业务外，不开展其他业务：
《战声》（War Voice），
《团结》（Unity），
《解放》（Emancipation），
《妇女》（Women）。

随后，本人去见汉文印刷厂印刷部经理王芝基（Wong Chi-gee）（第一被告）。1931年，当他在美成印刷厂（Mei Shen Press）担任会计，而本人在余庆里（Yu Ching Li，位于东熙华德路与新加坡路转角）做学徒时，本人便认识了他。王接受了这项业务。除了介绍印刷业务外，本人与这些秘密刊物无任何其他关系。

至于这些刊物的制版工作，

My name is Wong Dsu-chi. I am 18 years of age, a
native of Shanghai and single. I am a type-setter by
profession. I reside at Lane 587, 7 Medhurst Road.
I was an apprentice in the Tai Ping Yang Press,
Burkill Road, between August, 1935 and March, 1938. I
was thrown out of employment following the raid made by
the Municipal Police on the press on March 23, 1938, for
anti-Japanese literature. In May, 1938, I joined the

was operated by Bang Yuen-shen (3rd accused) and Ghui Pah

for the following periodicals only:-

1935年8月至1938年3月期间，本人在伯基尔路（Burkill Road）的太平洋印刷厂（Tai Ping Yang Press）做学徒。1938年3月23日，市警察因反日文学搜查该印刷厂后，本人因此失业。1938年5月，本人加入了由彭元成（第三被告）和瞿伯礼（第九被告）经营的、位于麦赫斯特路7号587弄的排字馆。该馆没有名称，仅承接下列期刊的业务：

My name is Fang Yu-ken. I am seventeen years of
age, a native of Ningpo and single. I am a type-setter
by profession. I reside at Lane 587, 7 Medhurst Road.

Prior to the raid made by the Municipal Police
on the Tai Ping Yang Press, Burkill Road, on March 23,
for anti-Japanese literature, I was employed in the Tai
Ping Yang Press as an apprentice. When Bang Yuen-shen
(3rd accused) established the type-setting works at Lane
587, 7 Medhurst Road, in May, 1938, I, being then unemployed,
went to work in this works. This works has no name and
carries out no business other than for the periodicals :-
"Unity" "War Voice"
"Emancipation" "Women."

Bang Yuen-shen (3rd accused) and Ghui Pah-lee (9th accused)
are in charge of the works. Ghui acted as the communication
agent between the works and one Tsai, who supplied money
for the upkeep of the works.

I was the person responsible for the dismantling
of set-up types when finished with and the placing of the
types in their original places.

I know that the printing of the periodicals was
undertaken by the Han Wen Press, Shantung Road and the
making of matrices was done by the Dah Foong Type-setting
Works, Wuting Road previously and the Lien Ts Type-setting
Works, Love Lane, behind the Bank of China Building.
About a month ago, I was sent by Bang to send set-up types
to the Lien Ts Type-setting Works for making matrices.
I have been there once only.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。

以下为第六被告、宁波籍人方餘根（Fang Yu-ken）之供词，由本人副督察麦阿迪（D.S.I. MacAdie）于1938年12月9日在特别支部（Special Branch）录取，并由副督察高仁肯（D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken，原文如此）传译。

本人名叫方餘根。现年17岁，宁波人，未婚。本人职业为排字工人。本人居住在麦赫斯特路7号587弄。

在3月23日市警察因反日文学搜查伯基尔路的太平洋印刷厂之前，本人在该厂做学徒。1938年5月，当彭元成（第三被告）在麦赫斯特路7号587弄建立排字馆时，本人当时失业，便去该馆工作。该馆没有名称，除为以下期刊服务外，不开展其他业务：
《团结》 《战声》
《解放》 《妇女》。

彭元成（第三被告）和瞿伯礼（Ghui Pah-lee）（第九被告）负责管理该馆。瞿充当该馆与一位蔡姓人士之间的联络代理人，后者提供资金维持该馆运作。

本人负责在排版完成后拆除活字，并将活字放回原处。

本人知道这些期刊的印刷由山东路的汉文印刷厂承担，制版工作此前由吴淞路的大丰排字馆完成，后来由中国银行大楼后方爱多亚路（Love Lane，即今延安东路旧称之一，此处指具体弄堂名或路段）的联慈（Lien Ts，音译）排字馆完成。大约一个月前，本人受彭派遣，将排好的活字送到联慈排字馆进行制版。本人只去过那里一次。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Tsang Vung Tsing (張文心) (8th accused)
native of Pootung taken by me D.S.I. MacAdie
at Police Hqrs. on the Dec. 13, 1938 and interpreted by D.S.I. Kao Yen-King.

My name is Tsang Vung Tsing. I am 20 years of age, a native of Pootung and single. I am a type-setter by profession. I reside at Lane 587, 7 Medhurst Road.

I was an apprentice in the Tai Ping Yang Press, Burkill Road, but was discharged owing to lack of business following a raid made by the Municipal Police on the press for anti-Japanese literature. In April, 1938, I went back to my native home at Pootung owing to the death of my mother. I returned to Shanghai in July, 1938 and joined the secret type-setting base operated by Bang Yuen-shen (3rd accused) at Lane 587, 7 Medhurst Road. This base sets up types for the following periodicals only:-
"War Voice", "Unity", "Emancipation", "Women."
In August, 1938, we set up types for the "Students' Livelihood" for one issue only.

At the time of raid on the Medhurst base on December 1, I was out to see a relative Chang Moh-ling (張木林), at the Chang Shen Shing (張順兴) Rice Shop, Weihaiwei Road, off Chengtu Road. When I returned to the base at 6 p.m., I met the wife of Bang (3rd accused) in the alleyway. She asked me to look for Ghui Pah-lee (9th accused) in the French Concession. At Ghui's residence at 907 Avenue Joffre, I was arrested. I deny that I went to Ghui with a view to reporting the matter to him and enabling him to make good his escape.

以下为第八被告、浦东籍人张文心（Tsang Vung Tsing）之供词，由本人副督察麦阿迪（D.S.I. MacAdie）于1938年12月13日在警察总局录取，并由副督察高仁京（D.S.I. Kao Yen-King，原文如此）传译。

本人名叫张文心。现年20岁，浦东人，未婚。本人职业为排字工人。本人居住在麦赫斯特路7号587弄。

本人曾在伯基尔路的太平洋印刷厂做学徒，但因市警察搜查该厂查获反日文学后，生意清淡而被解雇。1938年4月，因母亲去世，本人回到浦东老家。1938年7月，本人返回上海，加入了由彭元成（第三被告）在麦赫斯特路7号587弄经营的秘密排字基地。该基地仅排印以下期刊：
《战声》、《团结》、《解放》、《妇女》。
1938年8月，我们仅为《学生生活》（Students' Livelihood）排印了一期。

12月1日搜查麦赫斯特路基地时，本人外出到成都路附近的威海卫路张顺兴米店看望亲戚张木林（Chang Moh-ling）。下午6点本人回到基地时，在弄堂里遇到了彭（第三被告）的妻子。她让本人去法租界找瞿伯礼（第九被告）。在瞿位于霞飞路907号的住所，本人被捕。本人否认去找瞿是为了向他报告此事并帮助他逃跑。

-----

at Special Branch on the 8/12/38 and interpreted by

My name is Ghui Pah-lee. I am thirty years of age,
a native of Pootung, and single. I am a type-setter by
profession and reside at 907 Avenue Joffre. I together
with Bang Yuen-shen ( 彭元成 ) (3rd accused) operate a
secret type-setting base at Lane 587, 7 Medhurst Road, for
the secret publications entitled "Unity," "Emancipation",
"War Voice" and "Women".

Prior to April, 1938, I worked in the Tai Ping Yang
Printing Press, Lane 161, 11 Burkill Road, and was thrown
out of employment following a raid which was carried out by
the Municipal Police on the press on March 23, for anti-
Japanese literature.

In April, 1938, Tsai Lan ( 蔡磊 ) alias Li Yah-
yuin ( 李雅雲 ) whom I knew when he came to the Tai Ping
Yang Press and ordered the printing of the "Unity", gave me
and Bang Yuen-shen (3rd accused) $200 for the purchase of
types, which are now left at Lane 587, 7 Medhurst Road.
This secret type-setting base was established at the said
address in May 1938. We did not conduct business other
than for the above-mentioned secret publications. The works
was operated by me, and Bang Yuen-shen (3rd accused) assisted
by Wong Dau-chi ( 王如寄 ), (5th accused), Fang Yu-keng
( 方餘根 ) (6th accused) and Tseng Yung-tsing (8th accused),
who were apprentices. We were not paid according to the
amount of work done nor did we receive any wages. For us
five, together with the wife of Bang Yuen-shen who served
as a cook, Tsai Lan gave us $45.00 a month. Of this sum,

本人名叫瞿伯礼。现年30岁，浦东人，未婚。本人职业为排字工人，居住在霞飞路907号。本人与彭元成（第三被告）一起在麦赫斯特路7号587弄经营一个秘密排字基地，用于印制名为《团结》、《解放》、《战声》和《妇女》的秘密刊物。

1938年4月之前，本人在伯基尔路11号161弄的太平洋印刷厂工作，3月23日市警察因反日文学搜查该厂后，本人因此失业。

1938年4月，蔡磊（Tsai Lan），又名李雅云（Li Yah-yuin），本人在他来太平洋印刷厂订购《团结》印刷业务时认识了他，他给了本人和彭元成（第三被告）200美元购买铅字，这些铅字现在仍留在麦赫斯特路7号587弄。这个秘密排字基地于1938年5月在上述地址成立。除上述秘密刊物外，我们不开展其他业务。该馆由本人经营，彭元成（第三被告）协助，助手包括学徒王如寄（第五被告）、方餘根（第六被告）和曾永清（Tseng Yung-tsing，即第八被告，原文名字拼写与前文略有不同）。我们五人加上担任厨师的彭元成妻子，不按工作量计酬，也不领取工资。蔡磊每月给我们45.00美元。这笔钱中，

Translation of Petition from
Han Wen Printing Company.

The Han Wen Printing Co. Ltd has two departments;
the Business Department which manufactures and sells lead
types, and the Printing Department which undertakes the
printing of books, etc. The Company has carried on business
for many years, has always been law-abiding and has never
committed any offence, the promoting of its business is the only
object. In March last year, in consequence of difficulty of
control and in order to increase the efficiency of the printing
department, the whole of this department was rented to Messrs.
Wong and Loo who from that time have been jointly responsible
for all financial and business matters connected with it.
The name of the company was not changed but two characters
"Yah Kee" were added to the original name. On November 30
this year, the Yah Kee Printing Department was searched by the
Special Branch of the Municipal Police for having accepted certain
undesirable printing jobs, and the two men Wong and Loo who
were responsible for this department were taken into custody
by the Police. Both the Business and Printing Departments were
ordered to be closed. After explanation, the Police allowed
the Business Department to carry on but the Printing Department
is still closed. Although Wong and Loo are responsible for
the Printing Department, the property of this department belongs
to the Han Wen Company. Moreover the printing work is held up
and customers have complained to the Company for delays in
printing their articles. Two or three hundred workers are
idle as a result of the closure. For these reasons, it is
requested that the Printing Department be permitted to resume

汉文印刷公司请愿书译文。

汉文印刷有限公司设有两个部门：制造和销售铅字的营业部，以及承印书籍等物的印刷部。本公司经营多年，一向守法，从未犯有任何罪行，唯一宗旨即为促进业务发展。去年三月，鉴于管理困难，并为了提高印刷部的效率，将该部整体出租给黄先生和卢先生，自此以后，所有与该部有关的财务和业务事项均由二人共同负责。公司名称未变，但在原名后增加了“雅记”二字。今年11月30日，雅记印刷部因承接某些不良印刷业务，遭到警务处特别支部搜查，负责该部的黄、卢二人被警方拘留。营业部和印刷部均被勒令关闭。经解释后，警方允许营业部继续营业，但印刷部仍处于关闭状态。虽然黄、卢二人负责印刷部，但该部的财产属于汉文公司。此外，印刷工作停滞，客户因文章印刷延误向公司投诉。由于关闭，两三百名工人失业。基于上述原因，恳请准予印刷部在提供必要担保或在特别支部警官监督下恢复营业。

Translation of Petition from
Han Wen Printing Company.

The Han Wen Printing Co. Ltd has two departments;
the Business Department which manufactures and sells lead
types, and the Printing Department which undertakes the
printing of books, etc. The Company has carried on business
for many years, has always been law-abiding and has never
committed any offence, the promoting of its business is the only
object. In March last year, in consequence of difficulty of
control and in order to increase the efficiency of the printing
department, the whole of this department was rented to Messrs.
Wong and Loo who from that time have been jointly responsible
for all financial and business matters connected with it.
The name of the company was not changed but two characters
"Yah Kee" were added to the original name. On November 30
this year, the Yah Kee Printing Department was searched by the
Special Branch of the Municipal Police for having accepted certain
undesirable printing jobs, and the two men Wong and Loo who
were responsible for this department were taken into custody
by the Police. Both the Business and Printing Departments were
ordered to be closed. After explanation, the Police allowed
the Business Department to carry on but the Printing Department
is still closed. Although Wong and Loo are responsible for
the Printing Department, the property of this department belongs
to the Han Wen Company. Moreover the printing work is held up
and customers have complained to the Company for delays in
printing their articles. Two or three hundred workers are
idle as a result of the closure. For these reasons, it is
requested that the Printing Department be permitted to resume
business on furnishing the necessary guarantee or under the
supervision of an officer of the Special Branch.

Subject Arrests and seizure of National Salvation Propaganda at
587/7 Medhurst Road and the T'wan Wen Press - further
report.

Made by D.S.I. MacAdie    Forwarded by C. Crawford D.S.

Ghui Pah-lee ( 瞿百礼 ), the wanted communication
agent whose arrest was sought at 907 Avenue Joffre, was
taken into custody by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken at 2.45 p.m.,
December 4 in Room 411 of the Toong Fang Hotel, 245
Chekiang Road. The information leading to his arrest was
supplied by the family of the 7th accused Ya Sing Ling
( 葉平林 ), foreman tailor who was arrested following
his refusal to divulge information regarding Ghui Pah-lee.

On the afternoon of the same day, Ya Sing Ling
was released on the instruction of D.C. (Special Branch)
and was handed into the care of his step father named
Keng Ts-jing ( 子琴 ) residing 105 Rue Baron Gros.

Interrogation of Ghui Pah-lee age 30, native of
Pootung who now becomes the 9th accused is in progress in
an endeavour to trace the source of the propaganda matter
in question.

Results obtained will form the subject of a
further report.

The 9th accused is being detained at Gordon Road
Station.

瞿百礼（Ghui Pah-lee），即在霞飞路907号 sought arrest（寻求逮捕）的通迅联络员，于12月4日下午2时45分在浙江路245号东风旅馆411房间被副督察长高延肯（Kao Yen-ken）拘留。导致其被捕的情报由第七被告叶平林（Ya Sing Ling）的家属提供，叶平林是一名领班裁缝，因拒绝透露有关瞿百礼的信息而被捕。

    According to preliminary investigations the base
was established in Medhurst Road in July this year with
funds supplied by the national salvation association
and/or the Communist Party.    Type racks were built and
types to the value of $287 was purchased by the 3rd accused
and Ghui Pah Ling.    The plant was solely devoted to the
setting up secret national salvation and communistic
publications, in which work, the 3rd, 4th, 5th and 8th
accused and also Ghui Pah Ling assisted.    The printing
of the type blocks was done by the Han Wen Press, while
the making of matrices of the publication by the Dah
Foong Press, Lane 587/6 Wuting Road.    The four workers
referred to were all formerly employed in the Tai Bing
Yang Printing Press, Lane 161, No. 16 Burkill Road, which
was raided on March 23 by Special Branch for printing the
publication "Unity".    Together with Ghui, they received
a monthly allowance of $45 between them while their rent
was paid by the political association for which they were
working.    All four accused resided on the premises.
    Enquiries are continuing and observation is being
maintained at both addresses with a view to arresting the
communication agent Ghui Pah Ling or his brother Ghui Tsung
Nyi.

    Attached are lists of seizures made.

D.S.I. MacAdie, D.S. Hide, D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken, C.D.S.156
and C.D.C.357 (Special Branch), acting on information
obtained by Special Branch raided the Han Wen (漢文 )
Printing Press, Lane 228, House 15 Shantung Road.

three day periodical "War Voice" issue No.62 dated

the next issue of the paper.

Salvation organization.

Christian Students.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Assistance to Special Branch to visit the Han Vung ( 恆文 ) Printing Works, 15/228 Shantung Road re printing of anti-Japanese literature.
----------------------------------------
At 3.30.p.m. on 30.11.1938 D.S.Hide (Special Branch) requested assistance to visit the above printing works to search for and seize printing matter dealing with anti-Japanese activities. D.S.I.Guess and C.D.C.288 responded in conjunction with officers from Headquarters Special Branch but no books or other literature were to be found. Search of the premises, however, revealed several printing plates from which anti-Japanese leaflets had been printed and seven of these were seized and retained by Special Branch for further investigation.

Two persons were arrested and detained and gave their names as :-
(1). Wong Hsien Tse ( 王企峰 ), 41, Zaushing, M/Manager above address.
(2). Loh Cheu Sung ( 盧秋生 ), 45, Shanghai, M/Account. 6 Yue Shing Li, Rue Pere Robert, FT

These persons have, by order of D.C.(Special Branch) been detained in stations cells but will not appear before the Court at present. The printing works have been closed and S.P.Cs posted thereon during further Police enquiries.

At 4 p.m. on the December 1st, 1938, a member of
the Special Branch interviewed Mr. T. Hoggarth, Manager

according to a report received, desired to furnish in-
formation relevant to this case.

Mr. Hoggarth explained that Burroughs Wellcome
and Co. have a verbal contract with the Han Wen Press of
228/15 Shantung Road for the printing of Medical Diaries
for 1939 to the value of $2416.00 to be delivered not
later than December 10th 1938.

The diaries are intended for general distribution
in the Far East and in the event of delayed delivery, will
be rendered useless.

The Company has a further verbal contract for the
printing of Wellcome's Materia Therapeutica to the value
of $3570.00, but in respect of this order a delay of a
few weeks in delivery is not of great import.

Mr. Hoggarth further stated that on the afternoon
of December 1st, 1938, one Tsung Bah Oen ( 孫伯安 ),
General-Manager of the Han Wen Press had called on him to
explain that the Press had been closed by the Police and
that it appears unlikely that delivery of the diaries could
be effected on time.

Mr. Hoggarth stated that he thoroughly appreciated
the necessity of the adoption of appropriate measures, but
would be glad of information regarding the likelihood of the
Han Wen Press being permitted to resume operations in time
to complete the Diaries by December 10th. Crawford

上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. D. 登记处
档案号 9871
特别科分区号 38
日期 1938年12月1日。

主题：突袭山东路228弄15号汉文印刷厂——查获《战声》及其他反日和救国文献。
由 副督察 Hide 制作 经由 Crawford 助理局长转发

1938年12月1日下午4时，特别科一名成员会见了香港路60号 Burroughs Wellcome & Co. 公司经理 T. Hoggarth 先生，据收到的报告称，他希望提供与本案相关的信息。

Hoggarth 先生解释说，Burroughs Wellcome & Co. 公司与山东路228/15号汉文印刷厂有一份口头合同，为其印刷1939年的医疗日记，价值2416.00美元，最迟于1938年12月10日交付。

这些日记旨在远东地区广泛分发，如果延迟交付，将变得毫无用处。

该公司还有另一份关于印刷 Wellcome 治疗学手册的口头合同，价值3570.00美元，但就这份订单而言，交付延迟几周并不重要。

Hoggarth 先生进一步表示，1938年12月1日下午，汉文印刷厂总经理孙伯安 (Tsung Bah Oen) 曾拜访他，解释称印刷厂已被警方关闭，似乎不太可能按时交付日记。

Hoggarth 先生表示，他充分理解采取适当措施的必要性，但希望能获知汉文印刷厂是否有可能及时获准恢复运营，以便在12月10日前完成日记的印刷。 Crawford

In 1934, owing to the death of my grand-father, I returned to Canton. Two years later (1936), I came to Shanghai again and secured employment in the Editorial Department of the Shen Chow Kuo Kwang Zoe Bookstore, (神州國光社), 378 Foochow Road, as a proof-reader. I resigned from the position in March, 1937, and went to serve as a teacher in the Ming Ts (民智) Middle School, Weihaiwei Road, near Moulmein Road. Following the outbreak of hostilities in 1937, I was thrown out of employment. I joined the "Cultural Circles National Salvation Association," Pootung Guild Building, 1454 Avenue Edward VII. When I was studying in the Shanghai Law College, I made the acquaintance of a number of students who were communistic elements. A number of my fellow countrymen are also communistic elements. I preferred their company and I now admit that I am also a communist element. At that time I did not carry out any communistic activities, save for contributing articles of a leftist nature to the Chinese press. In October, 1937, Chang Ming-ts (張明之), who was a fellow countrymen and school-mate of mine, a communist element, introduced me to the 1st Refugee Camp of the International Relief Committee, Rue Massenet. keeps his residential address secret from those representatives.
The weekly meetings were held in modern style tea rooms in
the French Concession, during which drafts were collected
and arrangements were made for the time and venue for the
next meeting. On receiving the drafts, he compiled them
with my assistance. I also wrote articles should there be

除了自己撰稿外，潘还从各个“界别”的代表那里征
集文章。他代表“文化界”，并与总共五名的其他代
表举行每周会议。他们分别是（1）学生界、（2）劳
动界、（3）职业界、（4）妇女界和（5）教育界的
代表。我不知道他们是谁。只有潘知道他们。据我了
解，潘本人对这些代表也保密其居住地址。每周会议
在法租界的现代式茶室举行，期间收集稿件，并安排
下次会议的时间和地点。收到稿件后，他在我的协助
下进行汇编。如果某一期有空余版面，我也会撰写文
章。汇编完成后，我将稿件送至麦特赫斯特路的秘密
排版基地，并指示彭和瞿安排

Association" is very much complicated and secret. I only
know the part in which I myself was engaged. In November,
1938, Wong Ping left for Pootung owing to private affairs
at home, and has not returned to Shanghai.
The property of the secret type-setting base was
purchased by Pan Ts-ming for the sum of $200.00. From the
National Salvation Association, I and Wong Ping receive
$20 each per mensem while Pan gets $30 a month. Bang and
Ghui responsible for the printing were given allowances
according to work done.
Pan Tse-ming told me that the publication of the
"Unity" was undertaken by the Cultural Circles National
Salvation Association. It is a secret organization and
governed by a committee including Chang Chung-ling (張宗麟,
formerly a professor of the Shanghai University, and Liang
Sz-jung (梁士純), a writer. I understand that the
committee members are mostly leftist writers and educationalists
and that most of them with the exception of Chang, Liang and
a few others are not in Shanghai. I also learned that Chang
Chung-ling concurrently acted as the Chief of the Finance
Department of the Cultural Circles National Salvation
Association. He gave money for the purchase of types in
the secret type-setting base on Madhurast Road, and funds
for the printing of the "Unity." It was he who also paid us
allowances. Only Pan Ts-ming can get into touch with Chang,
whose address has been kept secret from me.

a box and deposited it in my cousin Tsai Ying's home on
Route Pere Robert, while I deposited a part of my documents
in the 1st Refugee Camp. Following Ghui's arrest, I
refrained from staying at my residence or from attending
the refugee camp. About a week later, I returned to live

The following is the statement of Chu Han-sung (朱杏生) (10th accused)
native of Shanghai taken by me D.S.I. MacAdie
D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken
at Special Branch on the 12/1/39 and interpreted by

My name is Chu Han-sung, alias Chu Woo Shang
(朱和尚). I am 37 years of age, a native of Shanghai
and married. I am the Manager and owner of the Lien Ts
(联智) Type-setting Works, Lane 140, 15 Love Lane.
I live in the same address.

In July, 1938, Pang Yuen-shen (彭元成) (3rd accused)
who was a trade acquaintance of mine, came to me and asked
me to make matrices for the publications "Emancipation" and
"Unity." I accepted and did the work up to the end of
November, 1938, when Pang was arrested by the Municipal
Police. The price for making a matrix is $0.12. The
usual price for such a work is $0.15, the cheaper charge
being made owing to Pang and I being friends.

As a rule Ghui Pah-lee (9th accused) carried the
set-up types to my works and after matrices were made, they
were taken away by Ghui to the printing press, the name of
which was kept secret from me. Although I know that the
authorities would object to the printing of communistic
and anti-Japanese matters and I did express the desire not
to take up the work, yet I accepted it because Pang begged
of me and assured me that he would take all the responsibility.

以下为朱杏生（Chu Han-sung）（第 10 号被告）之陈述，籍贯上海，由特别支部警探长 MacAdie 及警探长 Kao Yen-ken 于 1939 年 1 月 12 日取得，并由____翻译

我叫朱杏生，别名朱和尚（Chu Woo Shang）。现年 37 岁，上海人，已婚。我是爱多亚路（Love Lane）15 号 140 弄联智（Lien Ts）排版社的经理兼业主。我居住在同一地址。

1938 年 7 月，我的商业熟人彭元成（Pang Yuen-shen）（第 3 号被告）来找我，请我为《解放》和《团结》刊物制作铅版。我接受了这项工作，一直做到 1938 年 11 月底，当时彭被工部局警务处逮捕。制作一块铅版的价格为 0.12 美元。此类工作的通常价格为 0.15 美元，因我与彭是朋友，故收取较低费用。

通常由桂柏李（Ghui Pah-lee）（第 9 号被告）将排好的活字送到我社，制成铅版后，再由桂取走送往印刷厂，该印刷厂的名称对我保密。虽然我知道当局会反对印刷共产主义和反日内容，我也曾表示不愿承接此项工作，但因彭恳求我并保证承担全部责任，我还是接受了。

My name is Liu Dong Hui alias Liu Sz Bei (劉世佩).
I am 22 years of age, a native of Ningpo and married. I am
a broker in the Lien Ts (联智) Type-setting Works, Lane 140,
15 Love Lane. I reside in the works.
In the hot season of 1938, I noticed in the works
a man, unknown to me, negotiating with Chu Han Sung (10th
accused), the Manager of the Works, the making of matrices
for the secret publications entitled "Unity" and "Emancipation".
The works was only concerned in the making of matrices and
has nothing to do with the type-setting and printing or
binding of the publications. The work was done with the
entire sanction of the manager, and therefore I did not make
any effort to refuse the order, although I knew full well
that these publications were banned by the Settlement
Authorities.

我叫劉全桓，别名劉世佩（Liu Sz Bei）。现年 22 岁，宁波人，已婚。我是爱多亚路 15 号 140 弄联智（Lien Ts）排版社的经纪人。我居住在社内。
1938 年夏季，我注意到社内有一名我不认识的男子正在与社经理朱杏生（第 10 号被告）商谈，为名为《团结》和《解放》的秘密刊物制作铅版。本社仅负责制作铅版，与刊物的排版、印刷或装订无关。这项工作是在经理完全批准下进行的，因此尽管我完全清楚这些出版物被租界当局禁止，我并未试图拒绝该订单。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of LOH CHING YOONG ( 陸金榮 ), 12th accused
native of ............................................................taken by me D.S.I. MacAdie
..................................................................................D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken
at Police H.Q. on the 12.1.39. and interpreted by ........................................

My name is Loh Ching Yoong. I am 51 years of age,
a native of Kashan, Chekiang, and married. I am the
Manager of the Shing Nyih Press, Lane 177, 42 Chungking Road.
I reside in the same press.
In May, 1938, I began to undertake the printing
of the "Emancipation" ( 解放 ), "Unity" ( 團結 ), "Women"
( 婦女 ), and "Students Livelihood" (one issue only),
on behalf of Bang Yuen Shen (3rd accused) and Ghui Pah-lee
(9th accused). In July, 1938, I refused to continue the
printing because I was aware that such publications were
prohibited by the authorities. I understood that Bang
and Ghui entrusted the printing to some other firm which I
do not know (The Han Wen Press), but as they were not
satisfied with the printing of the other firm, they came
back to me in August, 1938, and begged of me to continue
the printing. This I did to the end of November, 1938,
when Bang was arrested by the Municipal Police.
The price for the printing of these publications
was cheaper. Usually, I charged $1.40 for the printing of
500 broad sheets of paper, whereas I made a charge of only
$1.05 to Bang and Ghui. There were 2 reasons for this
special treatment; firstly because they paid me in cash
on delivery and secondly because they claimed these publications
to be of a patriotic nature.
When printed, the copies were taken away by either
Bang or Ghui to a bookbinding firm, the name of which Bang
and Ghui never told me.

以下为陆金荣（LOH CHING YOONG），第 12 号被告之陈述，籍贯 ____，由警探长 MacAdie 及警探长 Kao Yen-ken 于 1939 年 1 月 12 日在警察总局取得，并由 ____ 翻译

我叫陆金荣。现年 51 岁，浙江嘉兴人，已婚。我是重庆路 42 号 177 弄新艺印刷所（Shing Nyih Press）的经理。我居住在该印刷所内。
1938 年 5 月，我开始代表彭元生（Bang Yuen Shen）（第 3 号被告）和桂柏李（Ghui Pah-lee）（第 9 号被告）承印《解放》、《团结》、《妇女》以及《学生生活》（仅一期）。1938 年 7 月，我因意识到此类出版物为当局所禁止，拒绝继续印刷。我得知彭和桂将印刷工作委托给了另一家我不认识的商行（汉文印刷所），但由于他们对那家商行的印刷质量不满意，他们于 1938 年 8 月又回来恳求我继续印刷。我便一直印到 1938 年 11 月底，当时彭被工部局警务处逮捕。
这些出版物的印刷价格较为便宜。通常，我印刷 500 张大纸收费 1.40 美元，而我对彭和桂仅收费 1.05 美元。给予这种特殊待遇有两个原因：首先是因为他们交货时以现金支付，其次是因为他们声称这些出版物具有爱国性质。
印刷完成后，副本由彭或桂取走送往一家装订厂，彭和桂从未告诉我该厂的名称。

The following is the statement of Loh Foh Sung (陸福生) (13th accused),
native of Kashan, Chekiang, taken by me D.S.I. MacAdie
D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken
at Police H.Q. on the January 16, 1939 and interpreted by ____________________

My name is Loh Foh Sung. I am 30 years of age, a
native of Kashan, Chekiang, and married. I am the assistant-
manager of the Shing Nyi Press, Lane 177, 42 Chungking Road.
I reside in the press.

In May of 1938, Bang Yuen Shen (3rd accused) and
Chui Pah Lee (9th accused) came to the press and arranged
with Loh Ching Yoong (陸金荣) (12th accused), the Manager
of the press and my father, for the printing of the
"Emancipation", "Unity" and "Women". My father and I knew
well that these publications were banned by the authorities,
but took the risk of accepting the order owing to lack of
business. In July, 1938, we realized the danger of police
action and refused to accept further orders. After an
interval of two months, Bang and Chui again came and begged
us to continue the printing. This we did up to the end of
November, 1938, when Bang was arrested by the Municipal Police.

Apart from assisting my father in the management of
the press, I was engaged in the work of printing these secret
publications.

我叫陆福生。现年 30 岁，浙江嘉兴人，已婚。我是重庆路 42 号 177 弄新艺印刷所（Shing Nyi Press）的副经理。我居住在印刷所内。

1938 年 5 月，彭元生（Bang Yuen Shen）（第 3 号被告）和崔柏李（Chui Pah Lee）（第 9 号被告）来到印刷所，与印刷所经理兼我父亲的陆金荣（Loh Ching Yoong）（第 12 号被告）安排印刷《解放》、《团结》和《妇女》事宜。我和父亲深知这些出版物被当局禁止，但因生意清淡，仍冒险接受了订单。1938 年 7 月，我们意识到警方行动的危险，拒绝接受进一步订单。两个月后，彭和崔再次前来，恳求我们继续印刷。我们便一直印到 1938 年 11 月底，当时彭被工部局警务处逮捕。

除了协助父亲管理印刷所外，我还从事这些秘密出版物的印刷工作。

(a) Narration entitled "Escape" by "Bah Wei"(白華 ),
(pen name). The following is a summarized
translation:-

ESCAPE

When the writer and one Mr. T., living
together, were discussing the sending of clothing
to one Mr. Zung being detained by the authorities
in connection with the "struggle for the
existence and independence of the nation", one
Mr. B. brought them the information that one
Lau Zee had also been arrested in a hotel. Lau
Zee was absent during a visit by the authorities
as he had expected the raid but his uncle, tailor
of a foreign clothing shop, was held in pledge.
The X X side demanded $2,000 for his release
should he fail to produce the wanted man.
Subsequently Lau Zee was induced to a hotel and
placed under arrest.
Following Lau Zee's arrest, Mr. B. advised
the writer to "clear up his room" and to conceal
himself at some friend's place. The writer then
told his female companion to bring a box to
Sister N's place and also informed her that he
would meet her there after he had visited Mr. B.
in a certain society for information.
- - -

student was warned by his school authorities for

逃亡

当作者与一位 T 先生同住，讨论向因“争取民族生存与独立斗争”而被当局拘留的 Zung 先生寄送衣物时，一位 B 先生带来消息说，刘子（Lau Zee）也在一家旅馆被捕。当局来访时刘子不在，因为他预料到了突袭，但他的叔叔，一家外国服装店的裁缝，被扣为人质。XX 方面要求支付 2,000 美元作为释放条件，除非他能交出被通缉者。随后，刘子被诱至一家旅馆并被逮捕。
